newsitem.title: UK: Chevron says agrees N.Sea asset swap with Statoil.
newsitem.headline: Chevron says agrees N.Sea asset swap with Statoil.

text.p: U.S. oil giant Chevron Corp said it and Norwegian state oil company Statoil have agreed to swap North Sea oil assets.
The principal part of the transaction is Chevron's acquisition of a 7.56 percent interest in the Draugen field in the Halten Bank area in offshore mid-Norway, Chevron said.
In addition Chevron expects to get a 30 percent interest and operatorship of license P157 and Statoil's remaining interests in three other Draugen licenses -- PL156, PL158 and PL176.
Chevron will also acquire Statoil's interest in Barent Sea licence PLl182.
Statoil in return will acquire a 12 pct equity in the Alba oil field in block 16/26 of the UK sector.
Chevron said it expects to complete other deals shortly as part of its strategy of growing its core areas in the central North Sea and west of Shetland.

Speaking of the deal with Statoil, Bob Connon, managing director of the Chevron Europe strategic business unit, said, "It is a major step towards implementing our corporate strategy of growing exploration and production in Europe."

Spencer Winter, director and general manager of exploration and ventures of Chevron, said the deal would give Chevron a strong foothold in Norway but did not mean there was no growth opportunity in the UK.
"We are adding a new arena by operating in Norway."
He said Norway offered good prospects, adding the businesss climate had recently improved, pointing to a lower cost environment and better licensing terms.
He said he expected further deals in Norway. "We are looking for things at least the size of this transaction".
